dedupe_keys.name: london green infrastructure framework lgif hex grid need and provision data

description: The London Green Infrastructure Framework, first published in January 2026, brings London-wide green infrastructure data together to evidence, plan and prioritise the green infrastructure Londoners need. The results CSV rates every cell of a hexagonal grid for ten strategic objectives, with separate need and provision scores and indicators that include access to parks and nature, blue cover and waterside access, flood zones and local surface water flood risk, river quality and road runoff, heat hotspots, tree cover, NO2 and PM2.5, cycling and walking routes, deprivation and resident groups such as young children, older people and social housing tenants, plus overall need and provision ratings. The analysis was developed by LUC for the Greater London Authority. The London Datastore hosts the downloadable results CSV (corrected version of 1 April 2026), a data dictionary, the hex grid shapefile needed to map the results, technical methodology and findings reports as PDFs, colour specifications and a change log, under the Open Government Licence v3; a web map is also available. Caveats: results are relative ratings on a grid, not asset records, and earlier CSV downloads contained errors. It supports climate adaptation, hazard exposure screening and planning of green-blue infrastructure; a related record is the Barcelona superblocks case study.
